title: Localization of point-section maps into completed-pullback cones
statement:
Fix the finite-field datum $p,a,q,k_0,k$ with $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$, a uniformizer $\varpi$, and $A_n=\mathcal O_E/\varpi^n$ for $n\ge1$ [def-trf-coefficient-conventions]. Put $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$, $g=\operatorname{Spec}(\gamma)$ for geometric Frobenius [def-weil-frobenius-detailed], $R=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,s}=\lim_n(A_n)_s$, and $\Gamma=\Gamma(s,-)$, with its constant $\mathcal O_E$-action, on the small pro-etale site in its module universes [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients, lem-weil-point-proetale-sections-exact]. For any flat-term K-flat complex $P$ of $R$-module sheaves [def-pc-kflat-complex, def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules], set $P_n=P\otimes_R(A_n)_s$, $r_{P,n}(x)=x\otimes1$ and $t_n=1\otimes(A_{n+1}\to A_n)$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum]. Put $C(P)_n=\operatorname{Res}_ng_n^*P_n$ with the actual coefficient-induced transitions $v_n$ of [def-weil-inverse-image-pullback-comparison](b), and $D(P)_n=\Gamma P_n$, $B(P)_n=\Gamma C(P)_n$. All towers are restricted to the single integral coefficient ring. For any strict tower $X$ with transitions $w_n$ put $s_X((x_n))=(w_nx_{n+1})$ and $H(X)=\operatorname{Cone}(1-s_X)[-1]$, with $H(X)^i=\prod_nX_n^{i-1}\oplus\prod_nX_n^i$ and differential $d(b,a)=(-db-(1-s_X)a,da)$ [lem-pur-integral-operations-well-defined]. For a strict tower map $f:X\to Y$ let $H(f)(b,a)=((\prod_nf_n)b,(\prod_nf_n)a)$. Let $c_X:\Gamma H(X)\xrightarrow{\sim}H(\Gamma X)$ be the normalized identity on both sectionwise product coordinates for a tower of $R$-module sheaves [def-trf-point-sections-roos-comparison].

Let $\mathcal P_R$ be the full subcategory of the homotopy category of $R$-module complexes on flat-term K-flat objects, with quasi-isomorphisms $W_R$ [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent]. Define $S(P)=[\Gamma P]$ and $T(P)=[H(B(P))]$, and on chain maps $h$ put $S(h)=[\Gamma h]$ and $T(h)=[H(\Gamma C(h))]$. Let $\overline S=\Gamma$ and $\overline T=\Gamma Lg^*$ on $D(R)=D(s_{\mathrm{proet}},R)$, where $Lg^*$ is the ambient completed pullback [def-pur-integral-derived-operations], with its specified representative comparisons [lem-pur-integral-operations-well-defined]. For a quasi-isomorphism $q:P\to N$, with $N$ any $R$-module complex, write $b_q:\overline T[N]\xrightarrow{\sim}T(P)$ for that comparison followed by $c_{C(P)}$.

The assignments $S,T$ factor through $\mathcal P_R$ and invert $W_R$. For every family of derived morphisms $\eta_P:S(P)\to T(P)$ which is natural for all chain maps between these representatives, there exists a unique natural transformation $\overline\eta:\overline S\to\overline T$ such that, for every $q:P\to N$ as above,
$$b_q\overline\eta_{[N]}=\eta_P[\Gamma(q)]^{-1}.$$
In particular the right hand side, transported back by $b_q$, is independent of the representative. For every roof $P\xleftarrow{a}Q\xrightarrow{b}P'$ within the resolving class with $a$ a quasi-isomorphism, both $S(a)$ and $T(a)$ are invertible and
$$T(b)T(a)^{-1}\eta_P=\eta_{P'}S(b)S(a)^{-1}.$$
This equation is independent of the roof presentation and expresses naturality for its arbitrary derived morphism. No completeness, boundedness or constructibility assumption is imposed.

proof.text: Use the proved product-preserving sections/Roos natural comparison from lem-trf-point-quotient-augmentation-diagram. Its two projection identities satisfy def-trf-point-sections-roos-comparison; uniqueness there identifies each component with the specified sectionsRoos. Compose integralDerivedPullbackComparison, exact sectionsFactors and this comparison to obtain the natural isomorphism d: L ⋙ G ≅ target, where L is Q restricted to the good complexes and G is completed pullback followed by sections. Exact sectionsFactors also gives e: L ⋙ F ≅ source.

Transport the functors Qh ⋙ F and Qh ⋙ G on the good homotopy subcategory through the componentwise comparisons F(quotientCompQhIso) ≫ e and G(quotientCompQhIso) ≫ d. Define the transported maps by conjugation. Naturality of quotientCompQhIso and e,d proves strict equality of their restrictions with source and target. Since Qh inverts homotopy quasi-isomorphisms, both transported functors invert that class. The same comparisons show that source and target invert every good chain quasi-isomorphism.

Use the existing proved goodComplexes localization theorem integralOperationsGoodLocalization_isLocalization from lem-pur-integral-operations-well-defined. Precomposition by L is fully faithful by lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property. For arbitrary eta:source→target take the preimage of e.hom ≫ eta ≫ d.inv. Its component identity is etaBar_[P] ≫ d_P = e_P ≫ eta_P. No invertibility of eta is used.

Expand the specified representativeComparison at q:P→N as G([q]^{-1}) ≫ d_P, using the normalized sections/Roos comparison. Precompose the desired equation with the invertible F([q]). Naturality of etaBar, then the component identity and naturality of sectionsFactors, gives the formula for every resolution. At q=id the formula recovers the component identity; localization natural-transformation extensionality proves uniqueness.

For a good roof, precompose the asserted naturality equation by source(a), apply eta.naturality to a, cancel target(a), and apply eta.naturality to b. For either comparison e or d, conjugation identifies inv(F₀(a)) ≫ F₀(b) with comparison_P.inv ≫ F(inv(L(a)) ≫ L(b)) ≫ comparison_Pprime.hom. Thus equal derived roofs have equal images for both source and target.

Apply DerivedCategory.right_fac to an arbitrary derived morphism, yielding an ambient chain roof K→P,K→Pprime. Resolve K by the flat-term K-flat resolution R→K of lem-pc-kflat-resolution and compose both legs. The denominator is a quasi-isomorphism by composition. Functoriality, inverse-of-composite and cancellation of Q(R→K) show that the resulting good roof represents the original morphism.

tool_uses.why: Exact sections at an algebraically closed pro-etale point preserve quasi-isomorphisms; this generic point-site fact is not supplied by the Weil-data unit.
The generic signed Roos construction carries transition-compatible homotopies to homotopies; the unit does not supply this cone-sign lemma.
The ambient completed pullback inverts good quasi-isomorphisms and supplies its specified natural representative comparisons; no Weil-data lemma supplies this construction.
Only its first assertion, that good K-flat homotopy representatives localize equivalently to D(R), is used; this general ringed-site localization tool is not specific to the unit.
The ambient homotopy category has the right calculus of quasi-isomorphism fractions, a general derived-category tool.
Arbitrary derived morphisms are ambient right fractions; this generic categorical tool is not a Weil-data proof route.
Resolve the middle complex of an ambient roof by a flat-term K-flat complex, without boundedness; this general ringed-site resolution theorem is not proved in the unit.
